title: The slow climb

alert.title: checkout: 5 restarts in the last hour
alert.summary: Customers see checkout errors every few minutes. Servers are being killed for using too much memory.

clues.title: Server events
lines: 10:02 checkout-7f9c  killed: out of memory (limit 1 GB)

clues.title: Memory per server, last 3 days
lines: Starts at 300 MB after a restart.
Climbs in a straight line to 1 GB, then the server is killed.
The pattern began Tuesday at 4 PM.

clues.title: Checkout requests per minute
lines: No spike before or during the restarts.

clues.title: Recent deploys
lines: Tue 3:52 PM  checkout v3.4.0: cache exchange rates for each request

clues.title: What changed in v3.4.0
lines: // nothing ever removes entries from rateCache

actions.label: Restart every checkout server
actions.feedback: Memory drops to 300 MB and starts climbing again right away.

actions.label: Raise the memory limit to 2 GB
actions.feedback: Servers now live about 50 minutes instead of 25. The leak is still there.

actions.label: Add more checkout servers
actions.feedback: Each server gets fewer requests, so it dies more slowly, but every one still climbs to 1 GB.

actions.label: Turn off payment retries to cut load
actions.feedback: Card charges now fail for good on the first error, and support tickets start arriving.

actions.label: Roll back to v3.3.2
actions.feedback: Memory stays flat at 300 MB and checkout errors stop.

rootCause.summary: Version 3.4.0 added a cache keyed by request that never removed entries, so memory grew with every request until servers were killed.
keyPoints: the v3.4.0 deploy added a cache
the cache never removed old entries
memory grew until servers hit their limit and were killed

lesson: Memory that climbs steadily after a deploy points to a leak in that deploy. Roll back first, then give the cache a size limit.
